title: In 1 John 5 What Does It Mean To Have Faith In The Son Of God And How Does That Faith Manifest In Our Lives
paragraphs: Understanding Faith in the Son of God from 1 John 5

The fifth chapter of First John is a profound exploration of what it means to place faith in Jesus Christ, the Son of God. This passage not only defines faith but also describes its practical outworking in the lives of believers. Let’s delve into the text and discover its rich theological insights.
1. The Identity of True Faith
Faith in the Son of God is not an abstract or general belief—it is a specific, personal trust in Jesus Christ as the incarnate Son, Savior, and Lord. John writes:
Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is begotten of God: and whosoever loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. - 1 John 5:1 ASV

To “believe that Jesus is the Christ” means to affirm that Jesus is the promised Messiah, the one sent by God to rescue humanity from sin. This belief is not mere intellectual assent but a heartfelt trust that results in spiritual rebirth—being “begotten of God.”
2. The Assurance and Victory of Faith
John emphasizes that this faith brings with it an assurance and a new identity as children of God. Further, it leads to victory over the world:
For whatsoever is begotten of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that hath overcome the world, even our faith. - 1 John 5:4 ASV

Faith in Christ is the means by which believers overcome the fallen world’s temptations, doubts, and opposition. The victory is not in our strength but in the object of our faith—Jesus Himself. This echoes Jesus’ own words:
These things have I spoken unto you, that in me ye may have peace. In the world ye have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world. - John 16:33 ASV
3. Faith as Trust in Testimony
John stresses the importance of believing the testimony God has given concerning His Son:

He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in him: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he hath not believed in the witness that God hath borne concerning his Son. - 1 John 5:10 ASV

Faith in the Son of God means accepting God’s own declaration about who Jesus is—His life, sacrificial death, and resurrection. Rejecting this testimony is, in effect, calling God a liar, which underscores the seriousness of unbelief.
4. The Manifestation of Faith in Daily Life
How does this faith show itself? John gives several practical outworkings:

Obedience to God’s Commands: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” (1 John 5:3 ASV) Genuine faith produces a desire to obey God—not out of duty but from love.

Love for Other Believers: “Whosoever loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.” (1 John 5:1 ASV) Faith in the Son unites believers as a spiritual family, manifesting in love for one another.

Confidence in Eternal Life: “And the witness is this, that God gave unto us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” (1 John 5:11 ASV) True faith brings assurance of eternal life, not based on our merit but on God’s promise.
5. The Role of Faith in Prayer
Faith also manifests in confident prayer, knowing that God hears us:
And this is the boldness which we have toward him, that, if we ask anything according to his will, he heareth us. - 1 John 5:14 ASV
Such confidence is rooted in our relationship with God through Christ and our trust in His Word.
Summary

To have faith in the Son of God, according to 1 John 5, is to trust in Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, and to embrace the testimony God has given about Him. This faith leads to spiritual rebirth, victory over the world, obedience to God’s commands, love for fellow believers, assurance of eternal life, and boldness in prayer. All of these are made possible not by our works but by God’s grace through faith in Christ:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
